record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: For an n x n positive semidefinite matrix A=(a_ij) and real q, define the q-permanent per_q(A) as the sum over permutations sigma in S_n of q raised to the inversion number of sigma, multiplied by the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}. Is per_q(A), as a function of q, monotonically increasing on the interval [-1,1]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an $n\times n$ complex (or real) positive semidefinite matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ and a real parameter $q$, define the $q$-permanent of $A$ by
$$\operatorname{per}_q(A)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n} q^{\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)} \prod_{i=1}^{n} a_{i,\sigma(i)},$$
where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)=\#\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n,\ \sigma(i)>\sigma(j)\}$ is the number of inversions of $\sigma$. Note that $\operatorname{per}_{-1}(A)=\det(A)$, $\operatorname{per}_{1}(A)=\operatorname{per}(A)$, and $\operatorname{per}_{0}(A)=\prod_{i=1}^{n} a_{ii}$.

Prove or disprove: for every $n\ge 1$ and every $n\times n$ positive semidefinite matrix $A$, the function $q\mapsto \operatorname{per}_q(A)$ is monotonically nondecreasing on the interval $[-1,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for the monotonicity of the q-permanent on [-1,1] for positive semidefinite matrices did not return a definitive resolution. Related work on q-deformed commutation relations (Bożejko–Speicher) and on permanental inequalities exists, but no source explicitly confirming a proof or counterexample of this specific monotonicity conjecture was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Bożejko–Speicher framework for q-deformations and positive definite functions related to q-permanents.
status_evidence.claim: Related background exists on q-deformations and positivity but does not resolve the monotonicity question.

status_evidence.claim: Related permanent inequalities exist but do not address q-monotonicity directly.
